title: Homotopy category of a coherent localization
statement: Use nerves, quasicategories, equivalence edges and coherent functor categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a quasicategory $X$, let $hX$ have the vertices of $X$ as objects and homotopy classes of edges as morphisms; homotopy is generated by $2$-simplices with a degenerate side, and composition is induced by inner $2$-horn fillers. An edge of $X$ is an equivalence if and only if its class is an isomorphism in $hX$. Let $C$ be an ordinary category and $W$ a subcategory containing all objects. Enlarge universes so $C$ is small. Let $L$ be a quasicategory and suppose $q:N(C)\to L$ satisfies the coherent localization universal property: restriction to $N(C)$ identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(L,E)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N(C),E)$ on functors inverting $W$, for every quasicategory $E$. Then $q$ is essentially surjective, and $hq:C\to hL$ exhibits $hL$ as the ordinary localization $C[W^{-1}]$, with its universal property for functors and natural transformations. The comparison commutes with $q$ and is natural for functors of pairs $(C,W)$.
